examples.question_text: Calculate the time difference between $A(22^{\circ}\text{S},125^{\circ}\text{W})$ and $B(48^{\circ}\text{N},35^{\circ}\text{W})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
examples.solution_text:
Both longitudes are west, so subtract. Latitude does not affect the time difference.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=125^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=90\div15\\&=6\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Calculate the time difference between $P(18^{\circ}\text{N},0^{\circ})$ and $Q(32^{\circ}\text{S},45^{\circ}\text{W})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
Calculate the time difference between $A(12^{\circ}\text{S},40^{\circ}\text{W})$ and $B(36^{\circ}\text{N},65^{\circ}\text{E})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
examples.solution_text:
The longitudes are on opposite sides of Greenwich, so add.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=40^{\circ}+65^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=105\div15\\&=7\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Two stations are at $(8^{\circ}\text{S},117.5^{\circ}\text{E})$ and $(24^{\circ}\text{N},65^{\circ}\text{E})$. Calculate their time difference in hours and minutes using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=117.5^{\circ}-65^{\circ}\\&=52.5^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=52.5\div15\\&=3.5\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

Convert the fractional hour to minutes.

$\begin{aligned}0.5\times60&=30\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

The time difference is $3\text{ h }30\text{ min}$.

examples.question_text: At Town $A(16^{\circ}\text{S},95^{\circ}\text{W})$, the local solar time is $10{:}20\text{ am}$. Find the local solar time at Town $B(42^{\circ}\text{N},35^{\circ}\text{W})$. Use $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=95^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=60\div15\\&=4\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$35^{\circ}\text{W}$ is east of $95^{\circ}\text{W}$, so Town $B$ is ahead. Add the difference.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }B&=10{:}20+4\text{ hours}\\&=14{:}20\end{aligned}$

It is $2{:}20\text{ pm}$ at Town $B$ on the same day.

Use longitude-based solar times and $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.

(a) A presentation starts at $6{:}40\text{ pm}$ Thursday at $A(54^{\circ}\text{N},25^{\circ}\text{E})$. When does it start at $B(28^{\circ}\text{S},145^{\circ}\text{E})$?

(b) A live broadcast starts at $7{:}15\text{ am}$ Tuesday at $C(30^{\circ}\text{N},125^{\circ}\text{E})$. When does it start at $D(46^{\circ}\text{N},10^{\circ}\text{W})$?
examples.solution_text:
(a)

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=145^{\circ}-25^{\circ}\\&=120^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$B$ is east of $A$, so add $8\text{ hours}$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }B&=18{:}40+8\text{ hours}\\&=26{:}40\\&=02{:}40\text{ Friday}\end{aligned}$

The presentation starts at $2{:}40\text{ am}$ Friday at $B$.

(b)

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=125^{\circ}+10^{\circ}\\&=135^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=135\div15\\&=9\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$D$ is west of $C$, so subtract $9\text{ hours}$. Add $24\text{ hours}$ to the negative result and go back a day.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }D&=7\text{ h }15\text{ min}-9\text{ h}\\&=-1\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=-1\text{ h }45\text{ min}+24\text{ h}\\&=22\text{ h }15\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

The broadcast starts at $10{:}15\text{ pm}$ Monday at $D$.

examples.question_text: A plane leaves $A(0^{\circ},47^{\circ}\text{E})$ at $8{:}30\text{ pm}$ Wednesday for $B(0^{\circ},107^{\circ}\text{E})$. The flight takes $7\text{ h }45\text{ min}$. Find the local day and time at $B$ when it arrives. Use longitude-based solar times and $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=107^{\circ}-47^{\circ}\\&=60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=60\div15\\&=4\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$B$ is east of $A$, so it is $4\text{ hours}$ ahead. First find the departure time at $B$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure time at }B&=20{:}30+4\text{ hours}\\&=24{:}30\\&=00{:}30\text{ Thursday}\end{aligned}$

Then add the flight duration.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival time at }B&=00{:}30+7\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=08{:}15\text{ Thursday}\end{aligned}$

The plane arrives at $8{:}15\text{ am}$ Thursday, local solar time.

examples.question_text: A ship leaves Port $A(12^{\circ}\text{N},130^{\circ}\text{W})$ at $9{:}45\text{ am}$ Monday for Port $B(20^{\circ}\text{S},170^{\circ}\text{E})$. The voyage takes $14\text{ hours}$. Find the time difference and the local day and time at $B$ on arrival. All times are longitude-based solar times. For dates, use Greenwich time plus signed longitude divided by $15$, with east positive and west negative; do not use the shortest angular separation.
examples.solution_text:
Use signed longitudes relative to Greenwich.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=170^{\circ}-(-130^{\circ})\\&=300^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=300\div15\\&=20\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

Under the stated date convention, Port $B$ is $20\text{ hours}$ ahead. First find the departure time at $B$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure time at }B&=09{:}45+20\text{ hours}\\&=29{:}45\\&=05{:}45\text{ Tuesday}\end{aligned}$

Then add the voyage duration.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival time at }B&=05{:}45+14\text{ hours}\\&=19{:}45\text{ Tuesday}\end{aligned}$

The ship arrives at $7{:}45\text{ pm}$ Tuesday, local solar time.
